full_judgment:
4. Petitioners on 30.5.90 filed written objection in the aforesaid O.C. Execution Case No.4 of 1990 contending inter alia that since the alleged purchase took place during the pendency of the suit she had no locus standi to proceed with the execution of the decrees as she was not a party in the original partition suit No. 148 of 1970 nor did she take any step to be added as a party in the suit. The judgment debtors had already obtained a decree for permanent injunction in respect of the suit property against the plaintiff of Partition Case No. 148 of 1970, and the said decree has subsequently been confirmed by the appellate Court. The execution case is evidently barred by limitation having not been filed within 3 years from the date of final decree. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the said order the petitioners move this Court and obtained the present Rule. Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that in view of the fact that the final decree was made 25.1.87 and the only application for execution of the decree has been filed on 27.3.90 i.e. after the lapse of 3 years 2 months and 3 days it is evident that the execution of the decree is clearly barred under Article 182 of the Limitation Act and as such the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in holding that the execution case is maintainable and the same has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He next argued that haying regard to the admitted fact that the Execution Case No. 4 of 1990 has been filed after 3 years of the passing of the final decree, it is evidently hit by the provision of Article 182 of the Limitation Act and as such the decree was non executable as being time barred. He further argued that having regard to the fact that since the execution of the decree dated 25.1.87 was never stays by any order of any Court till the filing of the Execution Case No. 4 of 1990 on 27.3.90 and the opposite party was not prevented from starting the execution case within the statutory period of limitation, it's that Section 14 of the Limitation Act is of no avail to the opposite party to avoid the application of Article 182 of the Limitation Act and as such the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order on an erroneous view of law and the same has resulted in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice. He lastly argued that the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in passing the impugned order without at all spelling out as to how Section 14 of the Limitation Act could save the apparent time barred decree and the same has resulted in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice:- 

 8. From the impugned order it is quite clear that the execution case was time barred but the learned Assistant Judge condoned the delay in filing the execution case under section 14 of the Limitation Act. Section 14 of the Limitation Act reads as follows: 

 "14. EXCLUTION OF TIME OF PROCEEDING BONAFIDE IN COURT WITHOUT JURISDICTION—In computing the period of limitation prescribed for any suit, the time during which the plaintiff has been prosecuting with due diligence another civil proceeding, whether in a Court of first instance or in a Court of appeal, against the defendant, shall be excluded, where the proceeding is founded upon the same cause of action and is prosecuted in good faith in a court which, from defect of jurisdiction, or other cause of a like nature is unable to entertain." 

 There is no doubt that the provisions of Section 14 of the Limitation Act provides for exclusion of time of proceeding bonafide prosecuted by a party in a Court which has no jurisdiction to entertain the proceeding and this section is available not only to proceedings of the courts of the first instance but also in the appellate Court and in execution courts. But there is nothing on record to show that the decree was put into execution within 3 years in a Court having no jurisdiction to entertain the same. From the impugned order it is quite clear that the decree was apparently barred by limitation and for that reason the learned Assistant Judge condoned the delay under Section 14 of the Limitation Act on an erroneous view of law and as such the same has resulted in an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice. It may be stated here that the present petitioners tiled written objection in the aforesaid O.C. Execution Case No. 4 of 1990 contending inter alia that the execution petition being Lime barred, it is unexecutable. 

 9. Mr. Saha in support of his contention has placed before me the case of Md. Abdur Rahim and others Vs. Sree Sree Gredhari Jeo reported in 27 DLR 72. in that case the provision of Section 48 of the C.P.C. and Article 182 of the Limitation Act were considered and it was accordingly held: 

 Both prescribe the period of limitation for the execution of the decree the Civil Procedure Code fixes the longest period whereas the Limitation Act earliest period to take the first step in execution and the subsequent steps known as steps-in-aid." 

 "Limitation Act prescribes the period of limitation which the decree-holder must take earliest in point of lime for execution, whereas Section 48 of the Code of fixes the maximum limit, but it does not prescribe the time for filing the first application or the subsequent applications for execution. The Limitation Act prescribes that an application for execution is to be made within 3 years from the dates mentioned in third column of Article 182. An application for execution has, therefore to satisfy first, Article 182 of the Limitation Act earliest period prescribed and then also Section 48 of the Code which prescribed the maximum period of Limitation. If the execution petition is hit by any of the two provisions it is to fail." 

 "It is well sewed that 12 years is to be counted from terminus quo mentioned in clauses (a) and (b) of section 48 (I) of the C.P.C. Although the period of 12 years has been fixed which has been termed as an outside period the decree must be kept alive under the Limitation Act and Article 182 requires the first application for execution to the made within 3 years of the decree and each successive application to be made within three years of the final order passed on the last application." 

 11. There is also nothing on record to show that the decree in question was stayed by any order of any court till the filing of the Execution Case No. 4 of 1990 and as such the opposite party No. 1 was not prevented from starting it during the statutory period of limitation.
